items.heading: Matka / Ghada water storage
details: The porous clay of a matka enables evaporative cooling, keeping stored water naturally cool.

items.heading: Earthen-pot cooking
details: Clay provides slow, relatively even heating and good heat retention, suited to long, gentle cooking.

items.heading: Iron kadai / tawa
details: Cooking in iron cookware can contribute some dietary iron to food, particularly moist or acidic dishes.

items.heading: Copper water vessels
details: Copper has documented antimicrobial properties that can help reduce certain bacteria in stored water.
Trace copper ions are believed in Ayurveda to support digestion and metabolism.

items.heading: Banana-leaf serving
details: Banana leaves have natural antibacterial properties and add a subtle aroma and flavor to warm food.
Serving on leaves avoided the need to wash dishes with limited water, and the leaves are fully compostable afterward.

items.heading: Sal-leaf plates
details: A traditional, fully biodegradable alternative to synthetic disposable plates.

items.heading: Stone grinding (Sil-batta / Ammi)
details: Provides controlled, gradual mechanical grinding of spices and chutneys without any industrial processing.

items.heading: Hand pounding (Ural / Okhli)
details: A traditional mechanical method for processing grains, pulses, and spices by hand.

items.heading: Clay tawa / chatti cooking
details: Traditional clay vessels give distinctive, gentle heat-transfer characteristics well suited to slow cooking.
